newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli bonds end slightly higher.
newsitem.headline: Israeli bonds end slightly higher.

text.p: Israeli dollar-linked bonds closed sharply higher in an otherwise quiet market on Thursday after the Bank of Israel intervened in the local forex trading, traders said.
* Unlinked government bonds (Gilon -- issued for four years): +0.03 pct to 100.83
* Bank of Israel short-term Makam bills: +0.03 pct to 100.54.
Volume was a low 101 million shekels, with linked and unlinked bonds closing only slightly higher.
"The market is very quiet and activity is low. Overall trading was mixed with bonds posting only mild rises," said Michael Weiss of Evergreen Capital Markets.

"Turnover in CPI-linked bonds was only 20 million shekels. The big institutional investors were very active buying bonds in December and now they have lowered their profile," said Zvi Hoffman of Meitav Securities and Investments.

Unlinked bonds and Makams also posted only mild gains. "The yield on the Makam for one year is now around 14 percent, which reflects hope for an interest rate cut of 0.5 percentage point latter this month," Hoffman added.

Dollar-linked bonds posted the sharpest rise of the day. The Bank of Israel began buying dollars in the local foreign currency market on Thursday after the basket of key foreign currencies to which the shekel is linked touched the bottom end of its official trading range.
"The dollar has reached the bottom from which it can only rise," Weiss said.
Traders noted that despite the relatively sharp rise in dollar-linked bonds volume was a low seven million shekels.
Note: Makams are zero-coupon unlinked certificates with durations of three months to one year. The Bank of Israel issues Makams to absorb liquidity.
